# KB3e: the 18-point cover question for F2^7 — narrowed to an exact finite remainder (outcome=partial, no new kappa)

Contributor: **Aaron Wang**, with help from opencode (substantial AI assistance in scoping, implementation, verification and writing; no model named; no independent human review claimed). No kappa, supplier, certificate or selected-frontier change.

## Change and mathematical scope

In the PR943 prefix-walk model ([PR 943](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/943) by Ross Richardson (RossRichardson)), a restored seven-source singleton word is universal exactly when its prefix set `P` covers: `P + P = F2^7` — every mask of `F2^7` is a pair-sum `a + b` of two elements of the set (self-pairs cover mask 0; the sumset is translation-invariant, so WLOG `0` is in `S`). [PR 2542](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2542) by Aaron Wang (navinor) excludes length 18 and claims "No 17-point set covers `F2^7`"; [PR 2773](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2773) by Aaron Wang audits it split-by-split; [PR 2870](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2870) by Aaron Wang closes the remainder rows `(5,1),(6,0)` with an exact odd-coverage Fourier/Parseval identity (parseval `696` versus allowed `504`, deficit `192`), completing the 17-point question at the set level.

This package (kappa-blocker KB3e, an authorized explicit-open-request scope change recorded in `TASK.json`) asks the immediate successor, PR 2870's open question 1: **does any 18-point set cover `F2^7`?** It is the deciding set-level object for the `f(7)` `L = 22` route: a cover keeps `L = 22` alive and supplies its needed prefix set; excluding covers kills `L = 22` outright. A parity split `S = A u B` has `A` in the even coset (s points) and `B` in the odd coset (t points); the counting-feasible 18-point splits are `(12,6)`, `(11,7)`, `(10,8)`, `(9,9)` and their mirrors. **Every 18-point split has s and t of equal character parity — exactly the case the PR 2870 squeeze does not reach.**

**Verdict: outcome (c) of the assignment, labelled `outcome=partial` in `TASK.json`.** No 18-point cover was constructed and no split was excluded. Each surviving split's exact obstruction is recorded below; the finite remainder is exact and enumerated.

## Verdict per split (exact integers)

| Split | Odd excess | PR 2870 squeeze | Parseval remainders (A, B) | Allowed per side | Deficit | Profile system | Rows after floors | Search best of 128 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| (12, 6) | 8 | none (equal parity) | 1248, 696 | none (vanishing possible) | non-positive | feasible (16 spectra) | 808 | 118 |
| (11, 7) | 13 | none (equal parity) | 1166, 798 | 21294 | -20128, -20496 | feasible (22 spectra) | 501 | 118 |
| (10, 8) | 16 | none (equal parity) | 1080, 896 | none (vanishing possible) | non-positive | feasible (50 spectra) | 251 | 118 |
| (9, 9) | 17 | none (equal parity) | 990, 990 | 36414 | -35424, -35424 | feasible (31 spectra, partly undecided) | 196 | 117 |

Controls: the same profile system reports `(11,6)` infeasible (reproducing PR 2870's exclusion exactly, including the `696/504/192` squeeze numbers) and `(10,7)` infeasible (consistent with PR 2773's census exclusion), and accepts the split `(4,6)` of a real 10-point cover of `F2^5` with no false contradiction.

## The layers and their exact obstructions

1. **Reduction lemma (PROVEN).** With `D = p + B` for any odd mask `p` (so `D` lies in the even group `E`), `S = A u B` covers `F2^n` if and only if `A + D = E` and `(A + A) u (D + D) = E`. Checked exhaustively over all 256 subsets of `F2^3` and on the real `F2^5` cover. Each split becomes a two-set covering problem in `E`, isomorphic to `F2^6`.
2. **Fourier/Parseval re-derivation with tracked deficit (PROVEN bookkeeping; no exclusion).** The PR 2870 squeeze needs opposite character parity; at 18 points it never holds and all tracked deficits are non-positive (table). The squeeze as an 18-point exclusion mechanism is DEMOTED; PR 2870 predicted this.
3. **Per-character profile system (CHECKED; two PROVEN consequences).** Necessary conditions: character parities; the odd-half identity `f_hat(u) g_hat(u) = rho_hat(u)` with absolute value of `rho_hat(u)` at most `E_o` and `rho_hat(u)` congruent to `E_o` mod 2; the even-half bound `f_hat(u)^2 + g_hat(u)^2` at most `s + t + 2P - 2^n` with `P = C(s,2) + C(t,2)`; Parseval on both sides; and the exact attainable sums of squares of `rho`. The constraints hold on every real cover of `F2^3` and `F2^4` (exhaustive witness battery) and `F2^5`. The system excludes no 18-point split, but the **no-vanishing sub-case is infeasible for `(12,6)` and `(10,8)`** (PROVEN): e.g. for `(12,6)` a no-vanishing spectrum is forced to 24, 8 and 31 characters of shapes (2,2), (2,4) and (4,2), giving `sum rho^2 = 46`, which no nonnegative integer `rho` of total 8 attains (attainable values are 8, 10, 12, through 40, then 50 and 64). So any `(12,6)` or `(10,8)` cover must have at least one character outside the span of the all-ones vector where one side's character vanishes.
4. **Pair-representation rows with census floors (CHECKED).** PR 2773's rows `(e_ex, b_ex, c)` extended to the four splits (its byte-vendored shape/draw primitives with a contingency-table pairing-sums replacement for its `O(m!)` pairing loop, validated equal to it wherever it terminates). Floors: 0 for 6 to 9 points (Sidon k-sets exist), 3 for 10 points (fresh-proven here), 5 for 11 points (reproduced walk), 3 for 12 points (counting). Remainders: 808, 501, 251 and 196 surviving rows over 120, 36, 28 and 45 distinct `(e_ex, b_ex)` pairs. The "small remainder" expectation of the 17-point case is DEMOTED at 18 points; these row lists are the finite remainder.
5. **Bounded construction search (CHECKED; scoped search failure).** The smallest falsifying instance — one covering set — was searched first: direct seeded local search at `k = 18` (200 restarts) tops out at 118 of 128 covered masks; the structured `(A, D)` searches per split (60 restarts each; the one bounded pivot after the direct search failed) top out at 118, 118, 118 and 117; a `k = 19` probe reaches 124 of 128, matching the maximum PR 2634 recorded for `k = 19`. Non-vacuity: the identical machinery finds 20-point covers in 5 of 5 short runs, matching [PR 2634](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2634)'s recorded abundance of 20-point covers and its own failure to find 19-point covers in 200 restarts. A failed bounded search is evidence about the searched domain only and is never an exclusion.

The four zero shards (k10 budgets 0/1/2, k11 budget 2) are receipt-validated, not re-walked; fresh k10-budget-2 and k11-budget-2 walks independently confirm the two load-bearing zero facts.

## Reproduce

Standard library only, CPython 3.12, from the repository root:

```sh
python3 -I -B research/f7-18point-cover-question-seed6d34356c/test_engine.py
python3 -I -B research/f7-18point-cover-question-seed6d34356c/verify.py quick
python3 -I -B research/f7-18point-cover-question-seed6d34356c/verify.py fourier
python3 -I -B research/f7-18point-cover-question-seed6d34356c/verify.py rows
python3 -I -B research/f7-18point-cover-question-seed6d34356c/verify.py search
```

Observed markers: `Ran 21 tests ... OK`, `PASS_F7_18POINT_QUICK`, `PASS_F7_18POINT_FOURIER` (378.5 s), `PASS_F7_18POINT_ROWS`, `PASS_F7_18POINT_SEARCH`. The heavy census anchors recompute via the byte-vendored PR 2870 driver (`anchors.py k10b3`, `anchors.py k11b4`; resumable, per-sub-shard receipts in `ANCHOR-PROGRESS.json`, one progress section per mode): observed `PASS_ANCHORS_K10B3 count=149990400 total_hist={'3': 149990400} shards=62` and `PASS_ANCHORS_K11B4 count=0 total_hist={} shards=62`. Registered replay metadata passes (`PASS_PACKAGE_METADATA_AND_PINS`).

## Labels

- **PROVEN**: the `(A, D)` reduction lemma; the vanishing-character necessity for the `(12,6)` and `(10,8)` splits; the deficit bookkeeping showing the PR 2870 squeeze cannot reach any 18-point split.
- **CHECKED**: every recorded anchor reproduced; the exact row tables after floors; the profile-system status per split (with the `(9,9)` step-cap region labelled undecided, never a proof); the bounded-search record with its non-vacuity control.
- **DEMOTED**: the direct extension of the PR 2870 squeeze to 18-point splits as an exclusion mechanism; the expectation of a small row remainder at 18 points.

## Scope, limitations and concurrent work

Set-level only, inside PR943's abstract interface. Not checked: everything word-level; the 19-point question; walk-realizability of any cover; any kappa, supplier, tariff or selected-frontier implication. The profile system supplies necessary conditions only — feasibility is never a construction. The gap `20 <= f(7) <= 24` is unchanged. The repeated-state `L = 20` word census (splits `(10,9)/(10,8),(9,9)` at the word level) is the concurrent claim of Nicholas Stone (NicholasStone, Kimi agent), [discussion 1166 comment 18954844](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-18954844); this package stays strictly on the SET-level object, its row tables cover the `(10,8)/(9,9)` set-level part of those splits, and `(10,9)` is a 19-point object untouched here. Pair-collision checks (discussions 1317 and 1166 with nested replies, before computation and again pre-submission) found no claim on the 18-point set object.
